subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw now supersede its April 5 localization deferral and sponsor RFC 0024's shared cross-surface localization contracts?
rationale: The RFC intentionally creates permanent product and compatibility contracts across several ownership areas, and repository evidence cannot determine whether maintainers are now ready to reverse the prior deferral.

options.title: Sponsor and calibrate RFC 0024
options.body: Confirm the initiative, resolve every listed owner decision in maintainer discussion, and preserve current metadata and stored locale behavior in the accepted contract.

options.title: Narrow the first RFC
options.body: Accept only locale identity and runtime message descriptors while leaving metadata and release coverage to later owner-specific RFCs.

options.title: Continue the deferral
options.body: Retain the existing surface-owned localization paths and pause or close the draft until maintainers initiate the broader program.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and calibrate RFC 0024
recommendation.body: Confirm the initiative, resolve every listed owner decision in maintainer discussion, and preserve current metadata and stored locale behavior in the accepted contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He recorded the latest explicit localization product direction and remains connected to adjacent onboarding and release behavior.
